Solution 8 (Pigeonhole Principle, very fast)[edit]

Consider any consecutive seven sets beginning on one more than a multiple of . There are guaranteed to be multiples of in these seven sets. Note that no set may have three multiples of . This means that some three of the ten sets have multiples of seven. There are such groups of seven sets, and then the sets and . These last two sets are congruent to and modulo 7, thus making it easy to check that each only has one multiple of . Therefore, there are sets with multiples of .
